subject.title: fix: harden security and release integrity

question: Should ClickClack permanently prohibit all private-network callback destinations, or preserve trusted self-hosted callbacks through an explicit allowlist or opt-in mode?
rationale: The PR changes an existing integration boundary from unrestricted callbacks to public-only destinations; code review cannot decide whether breaking trusted LAN and loopback callbacks is an intended security contract or an unacceptable upgrade regression.

options.title: Explicit trusted-private mode
options.body: Keep public-only callbacks as the default while allowing operators to configure narrowly validated private destinations with focused SSRF and upgrade tests.

options.title: Public-only contract
options.body: Intentionally reject every private destination and require migration documentation plus proof that supported deployments do not depend on LAN or loopback callbacks.

options.title: Split callback policy
options.body: Land unrelated hardening separately and pause callback egress changes until the trust contract is designed and reviewed.

recommendation.title: Explicit trusted-private mode
recommendation.body: Keep public-only callbacks as the default while allowing operators to configure narrowly validated private destinations with focused SSRF and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the strongest available security and release routing candidate and owns the proposed callback implementation.
